tool: M5.13 recorder (a raw WebSocket client in Python; sends only the guest namespace join and the Engine.IO ping 2 every 25 s, as the site's socket.io-client 2 does)
note: Direct, 150 s, the hottest broadcast of the hot timeline (about 315 listeners). Unlike S07-live, every content is kept whole: the room state 637 (every ~5 s, URL-encoded JSON with watchNumber), 636, entries 101/603, leaves 102, likes 210/211 and 7 chat lines. Viewers' uids, names and avatar paths became same-shape synthetic values (one person keeps one set of values across frames; the system sender 111111 and the anchor 2755394408455 are kept); the per-message hash s and the device id uxid in the sender's client string became synthetic hex of the same length; the Engine.IO session id became a synthetic one of the same form. Each level was decoded and re-encoded as the server writes it (event: characters outside the BMP as surrogate escapes; content: slashes escaped), so everything else is byte for byte the recording. Control frames are not recorded (the server sent none).
